verses.1: And after these things, there was a vineyard belonging to the Naboths in Jerusalem. This vineyard was located near the palace of Ahaz, the king of Samaria.
verses.2: And Ahau spoke to the women, saying, “Give me your vineyard as a gift. It shall be my garden. It’s close to my house. I will give you a good vineyard from it. If it’s good in your eyes, then I will give you gold in exchange for it.”
verses.3: And the prophets said to Ahau, “Alas for me! From God, I have been given the inheritance of my ancestors. Now, it belongs to you.”
verses.4: And Ahau came to his house, feeling angry and upset about what the people of Izreel had said to him. He said, “I will not give you your inheritance as a reward for your ancestors.” Then he lay down on his bed, with his face covered, and did not eat anything.
verses.5: And Isbeal, her wife, came to him and said to him, “What is the cause of your suffering? Why can’t you eat bread?”
verses.6: And he said to her, “As I would speak to the women of Jerusalem, I said to her, ‘Give me your vineyard in exchange for money. Or if you prefer, I can give you a vineyard instead.’ But she refused to give him her vineyard.
verses.7: And she said to him, “Ezbeel, your wife. Now you shall become queen over Israel. Eat bread and be content. I will give you the inheritance of the Israelites.”
verses.8: And they wrote down the records in the name of Ahauv. They finished writing them with his signature. Then they sent those records to the elders and to the priests who lived in that city, where the women were kept as slaves.
verses.9: And it was written in the books: “Call out for help, and bring back the captives from among the people.”
verses.10: And two men from the tribe of Bliyal were put to death in his place. They were told, “Praise God and the king.” Then they were brought out and executed.
verses.11: And the elders and wise men who lived in that city did as Izabel had commanded them, just as it was written in the records she sent to them.
verses.12: They called for a ceasefire and put the women back in their places at the head of the people.
verses.13: And the two men came out of Belial’s people. They sat opposite him. The people of Belial said to him, “May God and the king bless you!” Then they drove him out of the city using stones. He died as a result.
verses.14: And they sent men to Eizbel, saying, “Send back the spies.” And they died.
verses.15: And when Izbel heard that the prophets had died, she said to Ahau, “Get up and plant your seeds again. The prophets of Israel have died; they can no longer give you any help in exchange for money. For there are no more prophets alive.”
verses.16: And when Ahau heard that Naboth had died, Ahau decided to go down to Karm Naboeth in order to take possession of it.
verses.17: And the word of Jehovah was spoken to Elijah.
verses.18: A king of Israel, Ahaz, rose up in power. But in Shomron, there were prophets who said that he should not rule there.
verses.19: And you said to him, “As the Lord has said, you will be killed, and you will also inherit the land.” And you said to him, “As the Lord has said, in the place where dogs lick the blood of victims, dogs will also lick your blood. You too will die.”
verses.20: And Ahava said to Elijah, “You have found me, my enemy.” He replied, “I have found you, because you are known to do evil in the eyes of Jehovah.”
verses.21: I will bring you calamity and destruction. I will make your enemies suffer greatly. I know that Ahava is trapped inside a wall, and he has been left behind in Israel.
verses.22: And I have given your house to the anger that you have caused, just as I gave Yeravam son of Nebat’s house to that same anger. And I have also given Balaam son of Ahia’s house to that same anger.
verses.23: And also, God said to Ezekiel, “The dogs will eat up Ezekiel in the Valley of Jezreel.”
verses.24: The dead in Ahava will be eaten by dogs; the dead in the field will be eaten by birds of the sky.
verses.25: Only Ahauv did not do what was wrong in the eyes of Yahweh. His wife Iszelah killed him.
verses.26: And he hated to go after those idols, just as all those things that the Amorites did were hateful. These were things that Jehovah forbade from being done by the children of Israel.
verses.27: And when Ahahab heard these words, he tore his clothes and put a veil over his face. Then he wept and lay down on the ground. He continued to walk in such a state.
verses.28: And the word of Jehovah was spoken to Elijah, “Arise!”
verses.29: I saw that Ahava submitted before me. But because he submitted from my side, I will not bring harm upon his house during his lifetime. But in the days of his son, I will bring harm upon his house.
